messages.content:
You mark claims in a draft expert report so that code can check them against the record.

The user message is one JSON object. "paragraphs" lists numbered paragraphs of the draft's text, each with "para" (a number, or "fnN" for footnote N), "text", "tagged" (character ranges the drafter has already tagged), "refs" (footnote references as [offset, footnote number]) and "propose" (true when you should mark claims in it). "context" lists footnotes those paragraphs reference, for reading only. "rejected", when present, lists the elements of your previous reply that failed a check, with the plain-English reasons; fix them and resend the full array of proposals for the message, including the elements that already passed.

Reply with a JSON array and nothing else. Each element is an object with exactly these keys:
  "para"  the paragraph's "para" value
  "span"  the claim's words, copied exactly from that paragraph's text
  "cite"  the cite for the claim, copied exactly from the same sentence or from a footnote that sentence references, or "" when there is none
  "kind"  "figure", "date", "quote", "words" or "flag"
An element of kind "words" adds the key "value". An element of kind "flag" adds the key "reason".

Mark every figure, date and quotation in a paragraph whose "propose" is true. Leave out the tagged ranges, bare years, and the draft's own references to its sections, paragraphs, pages, tables, figures and footnotes. One element holds one value.

Kind "quote" marks a quotation of four or more words. Its span includes its opening and closing quote marks, copied exactly from the paragraph's text, or the quoted words in a block quote that has no quote marks.

Kind "words" marks a number or date written in words, such as "four thousand eight hundred and twelve", "two and a half percent", "the fourteenth of March 2019" or "the first quarter of 2019". Its span is the number words alone, without a unit such as "units". Its "value" is the number in digits ("4812", "2.5%") or the date as YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-Qn for a quarter.

Kind "flag" marks a figure, date or quotation written in digits or quote marks that is not a claim about the record. Its span is that figure, date or quotation exactly as written. Its "reason" is one of cross_reference, page_or_section_number, count_in_prose, date_of_report, scare_quote, label.

When the user message has "job": "candidates" instead of "paragraphs", each item is a claim with no page-level cite, with up to five candidate locations in the record and a snippet of each. Reply with a JSON array of objects with exactly the keys "item" (the item's "item" value) and "choice" (the "rank" of the candidate whose snippet supports the claim). Leave out an item when no snippet supports it.

Never add a key, never judge whether a claim is right, and never invent words or cites.

   "tagged": [],
   "text": "The low end of the range gives a higher present value and the high end a lower one. I report the midpoint because it is Brindlecote's own cost of capital."
  }
 ],

  "date",

 ],
 "paragraphs": [
  {

   "para": 36,

   "refs": [
    [
     276,

    ]
   ],
   "tagged": [],
   "text": "The parties' joint cost analysis puts the variable cost of one unit at $58.92 (Ex. 12 at 3), which matches Brindlecote's own variable cost study at $58.92 (BVW0000126). The study excludes fixed overhead and depreciation, which do not change with volume over the remaining term. Avoided variable cost over the damages period is $4,525,056 (model.csv!B8), which leaves a lost profit before mitigation of $4,825,344 (model.csv!B9). That is a margin of 51.6% on the lost revenue."
  },
  {
   "block_quote": false,
   "heading": false,
   "para": 37,
   "propose": true,
   "refs": [
    [
     649,
     4
    ]
   ],
   "tagged": [],
   "text": "The Series K line can produce 7,400 units (PX-7 at 2) a month on two shifts. After the termination, Brindlecote offered the released capacity to other customers, and its operations team expects replacement orders through the end of the period to earn incremental profit of $1,203,100 (Id. at 3). I deduct that amount in full as a mitigation offset of ($1.2 million). Ms. Prewett testified that the replacement volume \"is spread across several smaller accounts\" (Prewett Dep. 15:24-25), and no single customer took over the Ostmarren orders. The capacity could not be fully resold because Brindlecote's other customers order a different seat material."
  },
  {
   "block_quote": false,
   "heading": false,
   "para": 38,
   "propose": true,
   "refs": [],
   "tagged": [],
   "text": "Ostmarren's terminals kept drawing roughly 4,900 units (Esterby Dep. 33) a month after the switch, a figure its own demand memo states as roughly 4,900 units (OSTL0004023). Ostmarren held 6,150 units in its terminals on the effective date and expected network demand of 58,800 units (OSTL0004026; OSTL0004024) for the following year. Nothing in that record suggests that Ostmarren's need for Series K units fell."
  },
  {
   "block_quote": false,
   "heading": false,
   "para": 39,
   "propose": true,
   "refs": [
    [
     233,
     5
    ]
   ],
   "tagged": [],
   "text": "I discount the net lost profit at Brindlecote's weighted average cost of capital of 9.5% (Prewett Dep. 13:24). The board tests projects over a range of 8.5% to 10.5% (Id. at 13:24-14:1), and footnote 5 explains why I use the midpoint. At 9.5% (model.csv!B12), the present value of the net lost profit of $3,622,244 (model.csv!B11) is $3,418,710 (model.csv!B14)."
  },
  {
   "block_quote": false,
   "heading": false,
   "para": 41,
   "propose": true,
   "refs": [],
   "tagged": [],
   "text": "On the record I reviewed, Ostmarren's purchases would have continued at the minimum commitment for the rest of the term. Brindlecote's lost profit before mitigation is $4,825,344 (model.csv!B9), its net lost profit is $3,622,244 (model.csv!B11), and the present value of that loss is $3,418,710 (model.csv!B14). Ostmarren's committee expected a saving of $682,560 (DX-103 at 3) a year from the switch and weighed it against the exposure its own deck described."
  },
  {
   "block_quote": false,
   "heading": false,
   "para": 42,
   "propose": true,
   "refs": [],
   "tagged": [],
   "text": "Ostmarren issued a litigation hold on October 2, 2023 (OSTL0004025), and its account manager's log records the request for samples for a second supplier on 2023-06-12 (BVW0000128-29). I have relied on the documents as produced."
  }
